title: Prompt Optimization & Autonomous AI Agents
description: Master ReAct frameworks, Chain-of-Thought prompting, Tool calling, and multi-agent coordination.

questions.question: What does the 'ReAct' framework combine to enable effective autonomous agents?
options: Reasoning (Thought) and Acting (Tool execution) in iterative feedback loops
Reactive frontend components with Node.js backend websockets
Recursive auto-encoding with convolutional neural tensors
Reinforcement learning from human feedback without reward models

questions.question: What is 'Few-Shot Prompting'?
options: Providing the LLM with a few illustrative input-output examples inside the prompt
Fine-tuning the neural model with under 100 gradient descent steps
Limiting the maximum token response length to three sentences
Running multiple LLMs with voting consensus across tokens

questions.question: In LLM function/tool calling, what actually executes the external function or API?
options: The client application code using the arguments emitted by the LLM in JSON
The LLM neural weights directly make HTTP network calls from GPU memory
The vector database automatically triggers webhooks upon vector match
The browser JavaScript sandbox evaluates arbitrary Python scripts

questions.question: How does 'Chain-of-Thought' (CoT) prompting improve complex multi-step reasoning?
options: It encourages the model to generate intermediate rationalization steps before concluding
It concatenates multiple chat transcripts into a single vector query
It encrypts prompt inputs to prevent prompt injection attacks
It increases the learning rate of the base transformer layer

questions.question: What security vulnerability occurs when malicious user input overrides system instructions?
options: Prompt Injection
Buffer Overflow
Model Quantization Shift
Gradient Leakage
